topics.label: Introduction to cancer hallmarks and mutation progression
topics.groupedBecause: This topic frames the lecture by outlining the learning outcomes, the multi-step model of tumor progression, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations in extracellular receptor pathways and intracellular signaling cascades drive sustained proliferative signaling and survival.

topics.label: Blocks in terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells fail to exit the cell cycle and differentiate into mature functional cell types across hematopoietic and intestinal tissues.

topics.label: Evasion of programmed cell death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses the molecular mechanisms, particularly p53 and BCL2 family regulation at the mitochondria, by which cancer cells avoid apoptosis.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and stress-response pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells overcome telomere shortening and p53-mediated senescence barriers to achieve unlimited division, concluding the overview of growth-control hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics analyze altered tumor metabolism, focusing on the Warburg effect, tissue-specific metabolic rewiring, and metabolic gene mutations that generate oncometabolites.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the activation of new blood vessel growth required to supply oxygen and nutrients to growing tumors through the balance of pro- and anti-angiogenic factors.

topics.label: Mechanisms, dynamics, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the systemic dissemination of cancer cells, metastatic inefficiency and microenvironmental compatibility, and the genomic signatures of secondary lesions.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This topic closes the lecture by reviewing the convergence of cancer hallmarks, recommending further reading, and providing housekeeping for upcoming practicals.
